claim: Conventional methods to measure protein-protein interactions rely upon the law of mass action.
source: Yet, conventional methods rely upon the law of mass action and cannot measure many PPIs due to a scarcity of reagents and limitations in the measurable affinity ranges.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods in the abstract.

claim: Conventional methods cannot measure many PPIs due to a scarcity of reagents and limitations in the measurable affinity ranges.
source: Yet, conventional methods rely upon the law of mass action and cannot measure many PPIs due to a scarcity of reagents and limitations in the measurable affinity ranges.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods in the abstract.

claim: The METRIS assay utilizes rolling magnetic probes to measure PPI interaction affinities.
source: The mechanically transduced immunosorbent (METRIS) assay utilizes rolling magnetic probes to measure PPI interaction affinities.
evidence: This is the core methodological description of METRIS in the abstract.

claim: METRIS measures the translational displacement of protein-coated particles on a protein-functionalized substrate.
source: METRIS measures the translational displacement of protein-coated particles on a protein-functionalized substrate.
evidence: This describes the measurement principle of METRIS in the abstract.

claim: The translational displacement scales with the effective friction induced by a PPI.
source: The translational displacement scales with the effective friction induced by a PPI, thus producing a mechanical signal when a binding event occurs.
evidence: This describes the physical principle underlying METRIS measurements.

claim: The METRIS assay uses as little as 20 pmols of reagents to measure a wide range of affinities.
source: The METRIS assay uses as little as 20 pmols of reagents to measure a wide range of affinities while exhibiting a high resolution and sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated as a key advantage of METRIS in the abstract.

claim: METRIS exhibits high resolution and sensitivity.
source: The METRIS assay uses as little as 20 pmols of reagents to measure a wide range of affinities while exhibiting a high resolution and sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated as a key advantage of METRIS in the abstract.

claim: Low-affinity interactions are commonly leveraged in biological systems.
source: Low-affinity interactions are commonly leveraged, as is seen for multivalent recognition (Markin et al., 2010), readers of highly abundant proteins, and in protein allostery (Daily and Gray, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Recognition of the epigenome relies on the interplay between post-translational modifications like methylation, phosphorylation, and ubiquitination.
source: In particular, recognition of the epigenome is recognized to rely on the interplay between post-translational modifications (PTMs), like methylation, phosphorylation, and ubiquitination (Yau et al., 2017; McGinty and Tan, 2016; Patel, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Multidomain-containing proteins are often regulated by allostery through weak interdomain interactions.
source: Furthermore, multidomain-containing proteins are often regulated by allostery through weak interdomain interactions (Gladkova et al., 2018; Peng, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Virtually all commonly used techniques to measure biological interactions rely on the law of mass action.
source: However, virtually all the commonly used techniques to measure biological interactions, for example, like ELISA, FP, SPR, NMR, BLI, AUC, and ITC, rely on the law of mass action, and to measure protein binding affinities in the μM range and above, highly concentrated proteins or ligands are required (Xing et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods with citation support.

claim: To measure protein binding affinities in the μM range and above using conventional techniques, highly concentrated proteins or ligands are required.
source: However, virtually all the commonly used techniques to measure biological interactions, for example, like ELISA, FP, SPR, NMR, BLI, AUC, and ITC, rely on the law of mass action, and to measure protein binding affinities in the μM range and above, highly concentrated proteins or ligands are required (Xing et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods with citation support.

claim: High protein concentrations lead to thermodynamic non-ideality and proteins can aggregate, self-associate, and non-specific interactions occur.
source: Furthermore, high protein concentrations leads to thermodynamic non-ideality and proteins can aggregate, self-associate, and non-specific interactions occur, thus obfuscating the binding signal (White et al., 2010; Saluja and Kalonia, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: NMR is the gold standard method to measure weak interactions.
source: NMR is the gold standard method to measure weak interactions; however, in addition to requiring copious amounts of materials, the proteins must also be isotopically labeled, a single affinity measurement requires substantial instrument time and complex data analysis, and of all the methods mentioned is the lowest throughput.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about NMR.

claim: NMR requires copious amounts of materials and isotopic labeling of proteins.
source: NMR is the gold standard method to measure weak interactions; however, in addition to requiring copious amounts of materials, the proteins must also be isotopically labeled, a single affinity measurement requires substantial instrument time and complex data analysis, and of all the methods mentioned is the lowest throughput.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of NMR.

claim: BLI and SPR can measure interactions while using a small quantity of the immobilized partner, but the soluble analyte must be at concentrations above the Kd.
source: BLI and SPR are methods that can measure interactions while using a small quantity of the immobilized partner, however, binding is still governed by mass action and the soluble analyte must be at concentrations above the Kd; for weak binders, this can still use large quantities of materials (Helmerhorst et al., 2012; Weeramange et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of BLI and SPR with citation support.

claim: Determining the active fraction of protein is significant because the calculated affinity is a dependent variable of the protein concentration for most fitting techniques.
source: Several factors contribute to this limitation, but determining the active fraction of protein is significant because, for most fitting techniques, the calculated affinity is a dependent variable of the protein concentration (Jarmoskaite et al., 2020; Hulme and Trevethick, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: METRIS can measure a wide range of Kd values from 10-2 to 10-15 M.
source: Here, we present a novel approach to measuring the strength of biological interactions that is moderately high-throughput, requires a minimal amount of protein material, and can measure a wide range of Kd values from 10-2 to 10-15 M.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of METRIS in the introduction.

claim: METRIS was inspired by the rolling of biological cells, like neutrophils exhibiting haptotaxis on endothelial cells.
source: This technique was initially inspired by the rolling of biological cells, like neutrophils exhibiting haptotaxis on endothelial cells.
evidence: This describes the biological inspiration for METRIS.

claim: Neutrophil motion is driven by chemical or ligand gradients.
source: Neutrophil motion is driven by chemical or ligand gradients (Voisin and Nourshargh, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The PPIs between neutrophils and endothelial cells increase the effective friction between the two cells, allowing rotational motion to be converted into translational displacement.
source: The PPIs increase the effective friction between the two cells, allowing the rotational motion to be converted into translational displacement.
evidence: This describes the physical mechanism of neutrophil rolling.

claim: A higher affinity PPI between the roller and the substrate results in a larger translational displacement of the roller.
source: Thus, a higher affinity PPI between the roller and the substrate will result in a larger translational displacement of the roller.
evidence: This describes the relationship between affinity and displacement in METRIS.

claim: METRIS is not dependent on mass action because both the roller and surface have immobilized proteins.
source: Since both the roller and surface have immobilized proteins, the method is not dependent on mass action and requires approximately 20 pmols to measure PPIs regardless of their strength.
evidence: This explains why METRIS differs from conventional methods.

claim: METRIS requires approximately 20 pmols to measure PPIs regardless of their strength.
source: Since both the roller and surface have immobilized proteins, the method is not dependent on mass action and requires approximately 20 pmols to measure PPIs regardless of their strength.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of METRIS.

claim: METRIS reproduced well-characterized binding preferences for DIDO1-PHD and ORC1-BAH methyllysine histone reader domains.
source: Using the METRIS assay, we reproduced well-characterized binding preferences for two different methyllysine histone reader domains (Gatchalian et al., 2013; Kuo et al., 2012) and weak interactions between the E2 Ube2D (Buetow et al., 2015) and UBL-domains (DaRosa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with citations.

claim: METRIS measured weak interactions between the E2 Ube2D and UBL-domains.
source: Using the METRIS assay, we reproduced well-characterized binding preferences for two different methyllysine histone reader domains (Gatchalian et al., 2013; Kuo et al., 2012) and weak interactions between the E2 Ube2D (Buetow et al., 2015) and UBL-domains (DaRosa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a result with citations.

claim: The affinities measured by METRIS range between 10-4 and 10-6 M for the characterized interactions.
source: These affinities range between 10-4 and 10-6 M.
evidence: This describes the range of affinities measured in the validation experiments.

claim: METRIS measured the ΔΔGs for the phospho/methyl switch phenomenon in DIDO1-PHD.
source: However, we were also able to measure several weaker interactions between unmodified histone peptides, which allowed us to measure the ΔΔGs for the phospho/methyl switch phenomenon in DIDO1-PHD (Andrews et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a novel result enabled by METRIS.

claim: METRIS measured a weak interdomain interaction between the isolated UHRF1-UBL domain and SRA domain.
source: Finally, we also show that this method can be used to measure a weak interdomain interaction between the isolated UHRF1-UBL domain and SRA domain, which is known to control the E3 ligase specificity and epigenetic DNA methylation inheritance (Foster et al., 2018; DaRosa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a result with citations.

claim: The UHRF1-UBL and SRA domain interaction controls E3 ligase specificity and epigenetic DNA methylation inheritance.
source: Finally, we also show that this method can be used to measure a weak interdomain interaction between the isolated UHRF1-UBL domain and SRA domain, which is known to control the E3 ligase specificity and epigenetic DNA methylation inheritance (Foster et al., 2018; DaRosa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: The permanent magnetic moment of the roller couples with the applied magnetic field, producing a magnetic torque and subsequent rotation of the ferromagnetic bead.
source: The permanent magnetic moment of the roller, couples with the applied magnetic field, producing a magnetic torque and subsequent rotation of the ferromagnetic bead (Steimel et al., 2014; Sing et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the physical mechanism with citation support.

claim: The magnetic field is many orders of magnitude stronger than the strength of noncovalent interactions.
source: Since the magnetic field is many orders of magnitude stronger than the strength of noncovalent interactions, in this system the higher the effective friction between the rollers and the surface corresponds to larger translational displacement.
evidence: This explains why higher friction leads to more displacement.

claim: The effective friction is determined by the strength and density of PPIs between the roller and the coated substrate.
source: The effective friction is determined by the strength and density of PPIs between the roller and the coated substrate.
evidence: This describes what determines effective friction in METRIS.

claim: The rolling parameter (RP) is a dimensionless parameter that varies from 0 to 1.
source: The RP is a dimensionless parameter that varies from 0 to 1 where 0 is no translational displacement and one being a sphere perfectly rolling at a single hinge point and translating a distance equivalent to its circumference.
evidence: This defines the rolling parameter.

claim: A rolling parameter of 0 corresponds to no translational displacement.
source: The RP is a dimensionless parameter that varies from 0 to 1 where 0 is no translational displacement and one being a sphere perfectly rolling at a single hinge point and translating a distance equivalent to its circumference.
evidence: This defines the meaning of RP=0.

claim: A rolling parameter of 1 corresponds to a sphere perfectly rolling at a single hinge point and translating a distance equivalent to its circumference.
source: The RP is a dimensionless parameter that varies from 0 to 1 where 0 is no translational displacement and one being a sphere perfectly rolling at a single hinge point and translating a distance equivalent to its circumference.
evidence: This defines the meaning of RP=1.

claim: Both the rollers and substrate are coated 50× the theoretical number of binding sites to ensure virtually all sites are occupied.
source: As described in the Materials and methods, both the rollers and substrate are coated 50× the theoretical number of binding sites, so virtually all the sites should be occupied.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol to ensure saturation.

claim: The average RP on the avidin surface is 0.081 ± 0.004.
source: The RPs have a gaussian distribution (Figure 1E) and the average RP on the avidin surface is 0.081 ± 0.004 while on biotin we observed a RP of 0.918 ± 0.002.
evidence: This is a measured result shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The average RP on the biotin surface is 0.918 ± 0.002.
source: The RPs have a gaussian distribution (Figure 1E) and the average RP on the avidin surface is 0.081 ± 0.004 while on biotin we observed a RP of 0.918 ± 0.002.
evidence: This is a measured result shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The interaction between biotin and streptavidin has a Kd of 10-15 M.
source: The interaction between biotin and streptavidin is reported to be Kd=10-15 M.
evidence: This is stated as a known value from the literature.

claim: The weakest PPIs measured are in the 10-2 M range.
source: While it is impossible to know the true Kd value for a null interaction, the weakest PPI measured are in the 10-2 M range (Yoo et al., 2016) and enzymes with Kd values in the 10° M range have been reported (Bar-Even et al., 2011), so we assume that null interaction must be between 10° M and the concentration of water 5.5 × 102M, and we settled on 10°M as an estimation of the null interaction, which based on our subsequent fitting seems like a suitable assumption.
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: DIDO1 is responsible for interchanging between active and silent chromatin states in embryonic stem cells.
source: DIDO1 is responsible for interchanging between active and silent chromatin states in embryonic stem cells, and its chromatin localization is regulated through a phospho/methyl switch, where phosphorylation of H3T3 evicts DIDO1 from chromatin during mitosis (Fütterer et al., 2017; Di Lorenzo and Bedford, 2011; Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: DIDO1 chromatin localization is regulated through a phospho/methyl switch, where phosphorylation of H3T3 evicts DIDO1 from chromatin during mitosis.
source: DIDO1 is responsible for interchanging between active and silent chromatin states in embryonic stem cells, and its chromatin localization is regulated through a phospho/methyl switch, where phosphorylation of H3T3 evicts DIDO1 from chromatin during mitosis (Fütterer et al., 2017; Di Lorenzo and Bedford, 2011; Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: DIDO1-PHD has a preference for H3K4me3 > H3K4me2 > H3K4me1.
source: DIDO1 has a preference for H3K4me3 > H3K4me2 > H3K4me1 (Gatchalian et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The differences in rolling parameters for DIDO1-PHD interactions are all statistically significant.
source: While the overall change to the RPs is small, these differences are all statistically significant because the data set has good statistical power and small percentage errors (<5%) (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to statistical analysis.

claim: The log-log plot of Kd vs. RP showed a linear relationship between the three known DIDO1-PHD binding interactions to the methylated peptides (R2=0.995).
source: We noticed that the log-log plot of Kd vs. RP showed a linear relationship between the three known DIDO1-PHD binding interactions to the methylated peptides (R2=0.995).
evidence: This is a data analysis result.

claim: There is a linear dependence of the log of the RP to the log of Kd that spans roughly fifteen-orders of magnitude.
source: Overall, this experiment suggests that there is a linear dependence of the log of the RP to the log of Kd that spans roughly fifteen-orders of magnitude.
evidence: This is an inference from the data analysis.

claim: For most PPIs, the Kon rates are very similar, and thus the Kd constant is mostly dependent on Koff.
source: For most PPIs, the Kon rates are very similar, and thus the Kd constant is mostly dependent on Koff.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about PPIs.

claim: METRIS predicted Kd values for DIDO1-PHD were roughly twofold tighter than the published values.
source: Using this fitting method, we could reproduce the literature Kd values with high accuracy; all of the predicted Kd values were roughly twofold tighter than the published values (Gatchalian et al., 2013) and the fold difference between the different methylation states is similar (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a comparison of METRIS results to literature values.

claim: METRIS estimated the Kd for H3T3pK4me3 peptide binding to DIDO1-PHD as 340 μM ± 90.
source: Remarkably, we were also able to estimate METRIS-Kd values for the weak interaction between the H3T3pK4me3 peptide (340 μM ± 90) and the unmodified H3 tail (1200 μM ± 440).
evidence: This is a measured result from METRIS.

claim: METRIS estimated the Kd for unmodified H3 tail binding to DIDO1-PHD as 1200 μM ± 440.
source: Remarkably, we were also able to estimate METRIS-Kd values for the weak interaction between the H3T3pK4me3 peptide (340 μM ± 90) and the unmodified H3 tail (1200 μM ± 440).
evidence: This is a measured result from METRIS.

claim: This is the first energetic analysis of the DIDO1 phospho/methyl switch.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first energetic analysis of the DIDO1 phospho/methyl switch.
evidence: This is stated as a novel contribution.

claim: DIDO1-PHD has the greatest discrimination between non-methylated H3K4 versus H3K4me1 despite having the highest affinity for H3K4me3.
source: Thus, despite the DIDO1-PHD having the highest affinity for H3K4me3, it has the greatest discrimination between non-methylated H3K4 versus H3K4me1.
evidence: This is an inference from the ΔΔG analysis.

claim: Only 10 μl of 2 μM (20 pmol) is required to load the substrate in METRIS.
source: One of the significant advantages of the METRIS assay is that only 10 μl of 2 μM (20 pmol) is required to load the substrate and less is needed for the rollers, which is significantly less than any conventional method to measure PPI affinities.
evidence: This describes the reagent requirements of METRIS.

claim: Histone peptide microarrays require 500 μl of 0.5 μM (250 pmol) protein.
source: We compared METRIS to histone peptide microarrays, which is another methodology that can produce binding data with a minimal amount of protein (e.g. 500 μl of 0.5 μM [250 pmol] protein).
evidence: This describes the reagent requirements of microarrays.

claim: For DIDO1-PHD, microarrays could observe a statistically significant difference between H3K4me3 and the other methylation states, but there were no other statistically significant differences.
source: For DIDO1-PHD, we could observe a statistically significant difference between H3K4me3 and the other methylation states, but there were no other statistically significant differences (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, and Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is a comparison of microarray results to METRIS.

claim: METRIS is significantly more sensitive and quantitative than other common methods to measure protein affinities that use comparable amounts of reagents at low concentrations.
source: Given this result, METRIS is significantly more sensitive and quantitative than other common methods to measure protein affinities that use comparable amounts of reagents at low concentrations (i.e. ELISA and microarrays).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the comparison with microarrays.

claim: ORC1 functions in licensing origins of replication by discriminating H4K20me2 from H4K20me1 and H4K20me3.
source: ORC1 functions in licensing origins of replication by discriminating H4K20me2 from H4K20me1, a PTM on active chromatin, and H4K20me3 a repressive PTM (Bicknell et al., 2011a; Bicknell et al., 2011b; Kuo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: METRIS measured binding of ORC1-BAH to unmodified H4, which has previously not been detected.
source: Using the METRIS assay, we could also measure binding to the unmodified H4, which has previously not been detected.
evidence: This is stated as a novel result.

claim: H4 unmodified binding to ORC1-BAH was measured to be 44-fold weaker than H4K20me2 binding.
source: H4 unmodified binding was measured to be 44-fold weaker than H4K20me2 binding.
evidence: This is a measured result from METRIS.

claim: For ORC1-BAH microarrays, the only statistically significant difference is between H4K20me2 and the other peptides.
source: The only statistically significant difference is between H4K20me2 and the other peptides (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), although the trends do match the literature and METRIS values, including the signal for the unmodified peptide when compared to the other peptides on the array, which support our findings with METRIS.
evidence: This is a comparison of microarray results to METRIS.

claim: METRIS is a single particle method and the RP measurements are taken 36 times for each particle, giving it high statistical power.
source: This highlights another advantage of METRIS assay, since it is a single particle method and the RP measurements are taken 36 times for each particle, this method has high statistical power.
evidence: This explains why METRIS has high statistical power.

claim: The E2 Ube2D1 binds to ubiquitin noncovalently with an affinity of 206 ± 6 μM.
source: For example, the E2 Ube2D1 binds to ubiquitin noncovalently with an affinity of 206 ± 6 and we have shown that a ubiquitin-like domain (UBL) on the E3 UHRF1 can bind with higher affinity (15 ± 1 μM with NMR or 29.0μM ±1 with ITC) (DaRosa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The UHRF1-UBL domain binds to Ube2D1 with an affinity of 15 ± 1 μM with NMR or 29.0 μM ±1 with ITC.
source: For example, the E2 Ube2D1 binds to ubiquitin noncovalently with an affinity of 206 ± 6 and we have shown that a ubiquitin-like domain (UBL) on the E3 UHRF1 can bind with higher affinity (15 ± 1 μM with NMR or 29.0μM ±1 with ITC) (DaRosa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: METRIS can measure and distinguish interactions in the 10-4 M range without utilizing highly concentrated protein solutions.
source: Therefore we have demonstrated that METRIS can measure and distinguish interactions in the 10-4 M range without utilizing highly concentrated protein solutions, providing a simple method to measure weak interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion about METRIS capabilities.

claim: Previous studies provided evidence for an interaction between the UHRF1-UBL and the UHRF1-SRA domain, which is required for ubiquitylation of histone H3.
source: For example, the role of UHRF1 in controlling DNA methylation requires interactions between its domains (Harrison et al., 2016a; Gao et al., 2018; Gelato et al., 2014), and specifically, our previous study provided evidence for an interaction between the UHRF1-UBL and the UHRF1-SRA domain, which is required for ubiquitylation of histone H3 (DaRosa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: For the SRA-UBL interaction, METRIS measured an RP of 0.119 ± 0.004, significantly higher than 0.081 for an unmodified surface and 0.085 for ubiquitin on the roller.
source: For the SRA-UBL interaction, we measured an RP of 0.119 ± 0.004 for the particles, significantly higher than the 0.081 for an unmodified surface and the 0.085 we obtain with ubiquitin on the roller (Figure 4A and Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a measured result shown in Figure 4.

claim: This represents the first direct measurement of the interaction between the SRA and UBL domains of UHRF1.
source: This represents the first direct measurement of the interaction between the SRA and UBL domains of UHRF1.
evidence: This is stated as a novel contribution.

claim: The W2V mutation to the UBL had a significantly reduced RP to 0.098 ± 0.002.
source: We also tested a mutation to the UBL (W2V) that previous biochemical assays suggested is critical for the interaction (DaRosa et al., 2018; Foster et al., 2018), and W2V had a significantly reduced RP to 0.098 ± 0.002 (Figure 4A, Figure 4B, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a measured result shown in Figure 4.

claim: The METRIS-Kd values were less accurate with the global fit than with individual fitting.
source: However, the METRIS-Kd values were less accurate than with the individual fitting and we could not discriminate between similar strength binders in different sets of PPIs (e.g. between DIDO1 and ORC1).
evidence: This is a comparison of fitting methods.

claim: RP values obtained for different types of PPIs cannot be directly compared.
source: These results indicating that we cannot directly compare RP values obtained for different types of PPIs and that there is likely some structural difference in each system that is not yet accounted for.
evidence: This is an inference from the global fit analysis.

claim: There is likely some structural difference in each system that is not yet accounted for in the METRIS analysis.
source: These results indicating that we cannot directly compare RP values obtained for different types of PPIs and that there is likely some structural difference in each system that is not yet accounted for.
evidence: This is speculation about limitations of the current model.

claim: METRIS measures the effective mechanical friction induced by PPIs, which is fundamentally different than current methodologies.
source: METRIS, which measures the effective mechanical friction induced by PPIs, is fundamentally different than current methodologies.
evidence: This is stated as a key distinction of METRIS.

claim: METRIS can be advantageous to other approaches when measuring weak interactions because both binding partners are immobilized.
source: Here, we have shown that METRIS can be advantageous to other approaches when measuring weak interactions, since both binding partners are immobilized.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of METRIS.

claim: METRIS uses a very low concentration of proteins while maintaining high precision.
source: Thus, METRIS uses a very low concentration of proteins while maintaining high precision.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of METRIS.

claim: ΔΔG values provide a quantitative measure for the interplay between concurrent PTMs, a central premise of the epigenetic code.
source: These values are significant because they provide a quantitative measure for the interplay between concurrent PTMs, a central premise of the epigenetic code (Rothbart and Strahl, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Interdomain interactions can be difficult to quantify without very resource-intensive processes.
source: These types of interactions can be difficult to quantify without very resource-intensive processes, and limitations with the proteins themselves (yield or solubility) may make these interactions unmeasurable.
evidence: This is stated as a challenge in studying interdomain interactions.

claim: Pulldown assays, chemical crosslinking, and proximity ligation are qualitative, rarely produce quantitative data, and require mass spectrometry.
source: Currently, pulldown assays, chemical crosslinking, and proximity ligation are qualitative, rarely produce quantitative data, and require mass spectrometry (Richards et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: METRIS estimated the Kd for the UHRF1-UBL and SRA domain interaction to be 60 μM.
source: Here, we have measured a direct interaction between the UHRF1-UBL and SRA domains that we estimate to have a Kd 60μM (Figure 5B), however, the biological context for this interaction is between two tethered domains, so an absolute value is only partially relevant.
evidence: This is a measured result shown in Figure 5B.

claim: METRIS will provide additional new data to the field of protein biochemistry and could aid in the parametrization of computational binding score functions.
source: Thus, METRIS will provide additional new data to the field of protein biochemistry and could aid in the parametrization of computational binding score functions.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of METRIS.

claim: To translate, there must be sufficient magnetic torque applied to the rollers such that the PPI or other interactions between the roller and the substrate can be broken as they translate across the surface.
source: To translate, there must be sufficient magnetic torque applied to the rollers such that the PPI or other interactions between the roller and the substrate can be broken as they translate across the surface.
evidence: This describes the physical mechanism of METRIS.

claim: Force spectroscopy methods have measured the force of the biotin-streptavidin interaction to be 160pN.
source: Previous studies using force spectroscopy methods have measured the force of the biotin-streptavidin interaction to be 160pN (Florin et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The effective friction is due to intermolecular forces, but currently there is no model for how to relate the force directly to the rolling.
source: Still, the effective friction is due to these intermolecular forces, but currently we do not have a model for how to relate the force directly to the rolling.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the current understanding.

claim: The rolling parameter is not inherently dependent on the protein concentration, so long as the rollers and surface are saturated.
source: Several factors likely contribute to this robustness: (1) the rolling parameter is not inherently dependent on the protein concentration, so long as the rollers and surface are saturated.
evidence: This explains why METRIS is robust.

claim: The measurements have high statistical power (≈10 particles each with 36 RP measurements) and very low percentage error.
source: (2) The measurements have high statistical power (≈10 particles each with 36 RP measurements) and very low percentage error, given the high accuracy of the measurement and low uncertainty of many of the variables in the rolling parameter calculation.
evidence: This explains why METRIS has high statistical power.

claim: Multiple interactions between the bead and the surface amplify the friction, which may be necessary to measure weak interactions.
source: (3) Multiple interactions between the bead and the surface amplify the friction, which may be necessary to measure weak interactions, and likely limits the impacts of inactive proteins on the roller and substrate.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of METRIS.

claim: METRIS has limitations, such as the reliance on literature values for extrapolating and scaling the METRIS-Kd and the need to biotinylate the binding proteins.
source: However, METRIS does have limitations, such as the reliance on literature values for extrapolating and scaling the METRIS-Kd and the need to biotinylate the binding proteins.
evidence: This is stated as limitations of METRIS.

claim: With future development, a better mathematical model will be derived that describes the relationship between protein affinity and rolling parameter.
source: We envision with future development, we will derive a better mathematical model that describes the relationship between protein affinity and rolling parameter as many factors will contribute to the friction, such as the number of interactions per bead or the size of the protein interaction.
evidence: This is speculation about future improvements to METRIS.

claim: METRIS is expected to be of great use to researchers studying PPIs.
source: Despite these limitations, we expect that METRIS will be of great use to researchers studying PPIs.
evidence: This is speculation about the future impact of METRIS.

claim: The streptavidin-coated ferromagnetic particles have a nominal diameter of 10 μm.
source: The streptavidin-coated ferromagnetic particles, provided by Spherotech with a nominal diameter of 10 μm, are composed of a core of polystyrene and CrO2.
evidence: This describes the materials used in METRIS.

claim: The density of biotin binding sites per roller is on the order of 6 × 10^8 biotin molecules per roller.
source: The density of biotin binding sites per roller is on the order of 6 × 108 biotin molecules per roller which corresponds to a density of biotin binding sites on the order of 5 × 1010 binding sites per mm2.
evidence: This describes the surface density of binding sites.

claim: The substrates are avidin-coated glass slides with a ligand density of 1.1 × 10^10 ligands per mm^2.
